CAPITAL TERRITORY UNION COUNCILS (CONDUCT OF BUSINESS) RULES, 1979
CAPITAL TERRITORY UNION COUNCILS (CONDUCT OF BUSINESS) RULES, 1979
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part 11, 21st October 1979]
S. R. O. 959 (1)/79.-In exercise of the powers conferred by
section 102 of the Capital Territory Local Government Ordinance, 1979 (XXXIX of
1979), the Federal Government is pleased to make the following rules, namely
,----
1. Short title and commencement.-(1) These rules may be called the
Capital Territory Union Councils (Conduct of Business) Rules, 1979.
(2) They shall come into force at once.-
2. Disposal of business of a Union Council.-(1) Subject to
sub-rule (2), all business of a Union Council shall be disposed of at its
meetings or at the meetings of its sub-committees.
(2) The business of a union council, with regard to the following
matters, shall be disposed of by its Chairman, namely :-
(a) the execution of resolutions of the Union Council;
(b) the conduct of the day to day administration of the Union
Council;
(c) the execution of contracts on behalf of the Union Council,
(d) the execution of works by the Union Council;
(e) the appointment, promotion, leave, transfer, punishment and
removal of the staff of the Union Council whose pay does not exceed such limit
as may: be specified, by the Union Council with the approval of the Federal
Government;
(f) the supervision and control of the staff of the Union Council;
(g) the grant of licences, permits and sanctions;
(h) the operation of the Local Fund;
(i) the custody, maintenance, inspection, development and improvement
of the property vested in the Union Council;
(j) the acquisition, sale and disposal of property up to such
limit as may be specified by the Union Council with the approval of the Federal
Government;
(k) assessment, collection and recovery of taxes, rates, fees and
other dues;
(f) the receipt of amounts on behalf of the Union Council;
(m) the incurring of expenditure of any single items, not
exceeding such limit as may be specified by the Union Council with the approval
of the Federal Government;
(n) the custody and maintenance of records of the Union Council;
(o) the issuing of notices on behalf of the Union Council;
(p) the institution and defence of suits, complaints and other
legal proceedings on behalf of the Union Council;
(q) the compounding of offences under the Capital Territory Local
Government Ordinance, 1979 (XXXIX of 1979), and the rules and bye-laws made
thereunder;
(r) the conduct of correspondence on behalf of the Union Council;
(s) the custody of the common seal of the Union Council; and
(t) the doing of such other acts as are declared by the Federal
Government to be performed by the Chairman.
3. Meetings of Union Councils.-(1) The Chairman may, whenever he
thinks fit, and shall, upon a request in writing of not less than one-fourth of
the members of the Union Council, call an emergent or special meeting of the
Union Council.
(2) If the meeting requisitioned under sub-rule (1) is not
convened, the members concerned may move the Federal Government and thereupon
the Federal Government may convene the meeting at such time and date as it may
specify by a notice addressed to all the members of the Union Council.
(3) The Federal Government may direct that any matter specified by
it be considered by the Union Council within a specified period and the Union
Council shall consider such matter within such period.
4. Orders of Union Council to be made in its name etc.-Every order
of a Union Council-
(a) shall be expressed to be made in the name of the Union Council
concerned;
(b) shall be signed by the Chairman, or the Secretary or any other
officer authorised by the Union Council in this behalf; and
(c) shall be sealed with the seal of the Union Council.
